title: Musicians' clubs in Detroit and New York's Rhythm Club
summary: Band Box Club in Detroit and the Rhythm Club on 125th Street where bands booked players.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: On Adams Street, that's where it was. Adams. So all right I played there and then I had this card, you know, from there. Then they told me, when I told them I was going to New York, they told me to go to the Rhythm Club on 125th Street. That's where all the musicians used to meet up there, all the big bands. They'd book you out. They used to book us out. Book this band out, that band, this piano play, going with that band, you know what I mean? So they did that. Well then I got a study job playing in the beer garden there, white beer garden, like cavalry like then, you know. I played there for about I guess somewhere around about a year. And this man he sold his business out. And I didn't go back there no more to play there. Because a new manager had got me to see. Then from there I'd just go and play from place to place, all the bands. Travel with them and I had a chance to go.
Do you remember what band you played with in Detroit when you were there for that two months?

Oh no, no. Well you see they had so many different bands. I couldn't tell you exactly, because I wasn't with no one study band. If I go there like today, all right, they say listen, we see we always would meet up there. Whatever that band needs a piano player, they say well you go with that band. Meet up where? I didn't understand. If they band by the club. That's the club they had there for all the musicians to meet there. Oh I see. It's just like if you go meet at the Union Hall or something like that, you know what I mean? At that time they didn't have Union.
And the club in New York was the same thing? Yeah, it was the club.
